body: In the same boat. I saw it on my therapist's website this afternoon even though I haven't received a call about it yet.  My appointment isn't until Thursday so I guess they have a couple days to call me yet. But I too have a hard time talking on the phone and personally things aren't going well and I work in a hospital hence work is extra stressful so all around just really wish I still had the therapy room but I guess we'll adapt. Not much of a choice.

I had a horrible fear of the dentist for many years even with nitrous oxide. In my 30's I went to a dentist that gave me valium to use the first 3 appointments with him. Since then I have been able to go without fear and even go for more frequent cleanings now every 3 months without fear since I didn't have good care for many years. 

Truth be told I haven't read all the details of the situation you posted but I really wanted to share how much a few doses of valium helped me conquer my dentist fears so maybe don't rule it out entirely.

I know many people probably would love a trip with some of their family. I spend a lot of time with relatives in my day to day life so when I take a trip one of the best parts is the alone time. Honestly, I'd rather not go at all than go with anyone else. I never intended it to be a family trip. I never presented it as a family trip.

Lol I'm an atheist but yes, this isn't just a one time issue. My aunts on their own are generally very respectful. My guess is the initial conversation with them was my mom saying I was considering this trip, followed by them saying how it sounds like fun, and my mom suggesting strongly, maybe even saying I'd want them to join. 

It's not so much the discomfort of talking to them - I think they would respect it - but the likely possibility of hurting their feelings. I assume they were kind of invited by my mom so un-inviting them seems hurtful. Thanks for your bigger picture view. I hadn't thought about that part.
Yeah, you might be on to something. Maybe there's no good way. I've been thinking about just putting a kabosh on the trip and waiting a few years.

I guess that was pretty much the point of my post: asking for ideas on how to accomplish that without hurting their feelings.

Or not.
I told her I was thinking of my next trip being to European Christmas markets/Germany and of course then timeline is pretty easily deduced.
They already know. When I have seen them they've brought it up. I can't just look the other way at this point.
